title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 151
paragraphs: Now when the messengers from the Ionians and Aiolians came to Sparta (for this business was carried out with speed), they chose, before all others, as their spokesman the Phocaian named Pythermos. He put on a purple cloak, so that as many of the Spartans as possible might hear of it and come together, and having been introduced before the assembly, he spoke at length, asking the Spartans to help them. The Lacedemonians, however, would not listen to him, but on the contrary resolved not to help the Ionians. So the messengers departed. The Lacedemonians, having dismissed the messengers of the Ionians, nevertheless sent men in a fifty-oared ship, to find out, as I imagine, about the affairs of Cyrus and about Ionia. When these men came to Phocaia, they sent to Sardis the man of most repute among them, whose name was Lacrines, to report to Cyrus the saying of the Lacedemonians, bidding him do harm to no city of Hellas, since they would not permit it.
